root_causes.description: product-catalog exhibited a severe p99 latency spike to ~10,000ms (mean 7716ms) during the incident window while serving normal request rates (~1.87 req/s). The fault is a pure latency anomaly: error rate was 0.0, CPU (~0.027 cores), memory (~24MB), and pod restarts (0) were all normal, and the service is a leaf with no downstream dependencies, ruling out resource stress, crashes, aborts, and dependency failures.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.000, max=0.000 across the window

evidence.expected_baseline: request_rate ~1-3 req/s (normal load; latency not caused by traffic surge)

root_causes.description: frontend p99 latency also spiked to ~10,000ms (mean 7594ms) during the same window. Per the service topology, frontend depends directly on product-catalog, so this is latency propagation from the faulted product-catalog service rather than an independent frontend fault.

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog for latency-inducing code paths (slow data-store queries, artificial delays, lock contention) and review recent deployments/config changes to the service around 2026-09-16T07:46Z; roll back if a change correlates with the window.

Profile product-catalog request handling (e.g., enable debug/latency instrumentation on GetProduct/ListProducts handlers) to identify the exact slow operation, since CPU/memory are normal and the delay is likely in blocking I/O or injected latency.
Add strict timeouts and circuit breakers on product-catalog calls from frontend, recommendation, and checkout so a single leaf-service latency spike does not propagate as ~10s end-user latency.
Configure a p99 latency SLO alert on product-catalog (e.g., p99 > 500ms for 2m) to detect this fault class earlier, since error-rate-only alerting would have missed it (error_rate remained 0.0).
